text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the August 19 editions of Russia's newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Russia will have to close some of its sugar refineries if it fails to solve the problem of taxes, introduced in May, for sugar imported from Ukraine.
- The Russian government is trying to skim the cream from profits of the lucrative arms exports.
- Chechen officials have successfully used the situation with hostages to their advantage, says the paper.
- Russian farmers need about 10.9 trillion roubles ($3.4 billion) to harvest all grain this year.

- All negative experiences at the Mir space station are very useful for future space flights, says the government newspaper, adding that the dramatism of situatioin at Mir should not be overestimated.
- A controversial religion law vetoed by President Boris Yeltsin is still likely to be finally passed this year, says Justice Minister Sergei Stepashin.
- Russia's aluminium sector is ready for foreign investment after all major disputes in the industry seem to have been sorted out.
- An average Russian has been earning about 883,000 roubles ($ 150) per month in the last seven months, according to official statistics.
- The Russian government is planning to present the 1998 budget to the parliament for approval on September 1.
